feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence so far: iteration 0 (±0.03 m) had all trials off_track, with 1 to 2 line losses and max_error at the 0.06 m floor. Iteration 1 (±0.04 m, kp 6) still had about 1.05 losses per run, with max_error 0.062 to 0.069. Iteration 2 (±0.06 m) scored 272.25, with the oval at 55% finish, but the s-bend and slalom still had 0.6 and 0.95 losses per run. Span is still the main limit. I have adopted your ±0.08 m span at 0.04 m spacing and your 0.016 m footprint, and I scaled the weights to x/0.04. Decide the next change from the race: if s-bend or slalom line_loss_events stay at or above 0.5 with max_error near 0.06 m, the span is still limiting, so try a 7-sensor array at ±0.08 m with 0.027 m spacing. If oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25 (it was 0.267 in iteration 2), move sensor y from 0.05 to 0.03 with x fixed. If line losses are gone but rms_error stays above 0.03, the 0.016 m footprint is too coarse, so try sensor_size 0.012.
requested_changes: If s-bend or slalom line_loss_events stay at or above 0.5 with max_error near 0.06 m, try a 7-sensor array at x = -0.08 to 0.08 with 0.027 m spacing, keeping sensor_size 0.012. Evidence: iteration 2 had 0.6 and 0.95 losses per run with max_error 0.063 and 0.066 at the ±0.06 m span.

If oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25, move every sensor y from 0.05 to 0.03, keeping x and the other fields fixed. Evidence: iteration 2 oval steering_oscillation was 0.267 and iteration 1 was 0.275, both above the threshold.

If line losses are zero but rms_error stays above 0.03, change sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012. Evidence: iteration 1 rms_error was 0.024 to 0.031 with the 0.012 m footprint, and the 0.016 m footprint is untested.
